attribution.note: Marcus's own parenthetical 'Asterisk' in his post. It is not part of the Bupe material he quotes.

semantics.note: Firm present-tense statement about the models of the time. The normalised wording matches the source without adding anything.

contract.note: 'Not enough' has no stated threshold. The contract ties it to reliable reasoning beyond training examples, which the surrounding text supplies, and it avoids an AGI bar. This is an ordinary, fair reading. The Q1 2024 window is the evaluator's choice but is reasonable.

evidence.note: The GSM-Plus preprint (29 Feb 2024, inside the window) tested 25 LLMs. They resisted some perturbations but failed systematically on others: partial but insufficient generalization.
A May 2023 study finding GPT-4 to be a strong generalized planner when given debugging help. It is consistent with 'some degree' and does not show reliable transfer across unfamiliar variants.

reviews.rationale: Under the fair plain reading, a primary evaluation from the target quarter shows partial generalization alongside substantial, systematic failures on reasoning variants. The planning counterevidence fits 'some degree' and does not show broad reliability. Limitation: the evidence centres on math reasoning.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his post.

semantics.note: The sentence was split: this claim covers only the driverless-car half. 'This' refers back to the generalization and outlier difficulties described just before it. The causal claim depends on the premise that driverless cars were still just demos.

contract.note: Reading 'just demos' as having no routine public driverless service is the ordinary reading. The contract explicitly avoids treating a limited service area as a demo. The Q1 2024 window is reasonable for a present-tense claim made in April 2024.

evidence.note: Waymo's January 2024 regulatory filing describes thousands of daily public driverless rides and over a million to date. It is an operator disclosure, a source type the contract accepts, made under CPUC deployment authority.
Waymo blog post: freeway riding was still employee-only, so deployment had limits. The post also says the public Waymo One service was operating in three cities.

reviews.rationale: The causal claim rests on driverless cars being 'still just demos'. In the target period, Waymo ran a routine public driverless ride-hailing service, which meets the contract's contradiction condition. Limited geography and freeway testing do not turn that service into a demo. Whether generalization limits slowed expansion is not settled, but the stated effect did not hold.

attribution.note: Marcus's own opening sentence in his post.

semantics.note: The 'dominant configurations over three decades' qualifier is kept. 'Have trouble' is correctly treated as difficulty, not impossibility.

contract.note: The contract reads the undefined 'surrounding space' as materially unfamiliar inputs or distributions rather than a literal convex hull. That is the ordinary reading and fair to the speaker; a literal geometric reading would change the result.

evidence.note: WILDS (2021): standard training gives substantially lower out-of-distribution than in-distribution performance on all 10 datasets.
Proves that common sum-based GNNs extrapolate poorly. It also shows that tailored architectures and diverse training data can succeed.
Shows high-dimensional learning is nearly always outside the convex hull. This undercuts a literal geometric reading, not the distribution-shift reading.
Systematic generalization achieved with specially designed meta-learning, not the conventional dominant training. It limits a universal reading but leaves the recurring difficulty intact.

reviews.rationale: Under the fair plain reading, primary research shows substantial, recurring performance loss under distribution shift and extrapolation for standard neural configurations. The counterevidence shows success only with tailored methods or challenges a literal geometric reading. Neither undermines the claim of recurring difficulty.

attribution.note: Marcus's own 'In short' summary sentence, followed by his own asterisk. The packet treats it as endorsed authorial text, not a quotation of Bupe.

semantics.note: 'What we can expect' is unhedged expectation, so it counts as a scored forecast. The context, a preprint on data and scaling, supports reading it as about data scaling. No horizon is stated.

contract.note: Reading diminishing returns as smaller marginal gains per unit of comparable data is ordinary and fair. The metric, scope and horizon are unstated, and the contract flags this.

evidence.note: A 2023 study, before the forecast, on repeated-data saturation. It concerns repeated tokens, not added unique data.
An April 2026 study reporting diminishing returns from more data, but only for a tiny attention-only decoder. It is not representative of the intended scope.
A May 2026 study finding sparsity delays saturation under repeated data. It qualifies the trend without showing returns stop diminishing.

reviews.rationale: The forecast has no deadline, and the evidence does not meet the early-resolution rule: no replicated, representative body of results at larger scales. The evidence covers small-model or repeated-data settings only. It cannot be scored before a conclusive event.
